modules.note: On a planet (lat/lon): the craters core does not have. Discs only -- a rim is a lighter disc under a darker floor; rays are tapering chains of faint ejecta.
On a planet: high ground. A lit flank (trim) beside its own shadow (panel), so relief reads under the body's light; a range bends, a spur dwindles.
On a planet: ground pulled apart. A dark chain of floors between lighter shoulders; the line is what makes it a canyon and not a crater field.
On a planet: a cone and its caldera. Dormant it is only relief; active, the caldera is a light, so it glows on the night side, and lava may run down a flank.
On a planet: molten rock. It is a light -- it makes its own colour and shows on the night side -- crusted over with dark discs so it reads as flowing, not as a lamp. A tongue narrows as it runs.
On a planet: frozen water. Nearly white, with a blue that only shows where it is deep or cracked. A patch, not the cap itself -- a cap is a band.
On a planet: open water with a coast. The shore is a lighter disc just larger than the water; a shelf is a paler blue between them.
On a planet: land in water. Each island is a pale shore under a green or brown body; the water they stand in belongs to the planet, not to them.
On a planet: weather that turns. Pale arms that curl and thin round a darker eye; it rides the surface, so it goes by as the planet turns.
On a planet: weather that drifts. White and translucent, so the ground shows through; a set of overlapping discs, never one.
On a planet, near a pole: charged air glowing. A light that shows only on the night side -- a curtain that bends round the pole, never a lamp.
On a planet: a mining base. The pit is the point of it -- a dark hole stepped down in tiers -- with domes and pads beside it and one work lamp.
On a planet: a handful of people far from anyone. Domes clustered for warmth, a pad, one lamp.
On a planet: a city. By day a pale smudge of built ground; by night a few clusters of lamps -- the light is what says people, and it shows only in the dark.
On a planet: where ships come down. A cleared field, pads in a row, and a beacon you see before anything else.
On a planet: somebody lived here once. The plan of a settlement, broken and dark -- no lights at all, which is the whole of the story.
On a planet: a machine remaking the air. A tower with a glow at its heart, and the haze it breathes out widening downwind.
